## Your own percentile {#find-your-own-percentile .smaller}

::: {.small}
- Rerun `try_spec()` with the choices that you submitted in Task 4, in the IDE workspace or in the webR workspace: its output includes your **placement**
- The placement is the share of the `r format(nrow(spec_curve), big.mark = ",")` specifications on the curve with a more negative claim-aligned *r* than yours. For the reproduced specification it is `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(spec_curve$r_ca < curve_ref$r_ca))`
- The same statistic that places the reference results, computed for **you**
:::

::: notes
Rerun `try_spec()` with the choices that you submitted, in your IDE workspace or in the webR workspace, whichever you have open. The placement line in its output is the statistic that places the reference results, the share of the eight hundred and sixty-four specifications on the curve that are more negative than yours. For the reproduced specification, my own model, it is sixty-seven per cent, so if you did not submit, that is your number. A sentence such as "my estimate sits at the Nth percentile of the specification curve" is a publishable way to report a robustness check, provided that you say how the curve was built.
:::
